archetype.name: Pocket Passer (downfield)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower who does his damage from the pocket on intermediate and deep throws. His legs have all but vanished from his game this year, so his value runs almost entirely through his arm and the volume his offense asks of it.

report.headline: Top-four yardage built on a dead run game, and the efficiency is returning
report.take:
Jordan Love is fourth in passing yards per game at 279.7, up 54.3 a game from last season, and second in total yards. Most of that is circumstance. Green Bay's rushing offense is last in the league in EPA per play at -0.291, and LaFleur's offense passes 2.2 points more often than situation predicts, sixth-most. Love is throwing about 39 times a game because the Packers can't run, not because they are blowing teams out. The rate stats are more ordinary. His EPA per dropback of 0.121 ranks 17th and his CPOE of -2.37 ranks 34th of 45. That is a long way from 2025, when he was fifth in EPA per play with a +5.5 CPOE.

The season splits into two halves. Weeks 1 through 3 were rough: -2.7 passing EPA at Minnesota under 47.8% pressure against what is now the league's best defense, -3.2 with a -13.6 CPOE against the Jets, then a 53-attempt chase in a 14-35 loss to Atlanta. Since then he has been positive in every game, including a 16.9-EPA, +16.2-CPOE dismantling of Chicago. Over his last three games he is at 0.243 EPA per dropback with a +3.3 CPOE, which is the 2023 to 2025 version of him. The last two came against Dallas and Detroit, defenses now ranked 30th and 31st, so some of that rebound is the schedule, but the early slump also came against strong or competent defenses.

The split that defines him is depth. Throws of 10+ air yards produce 0.486 EPA per attempt, and they account for nearly all of his passing value despite a 44.6% completion rate. Throws under 10 yards barely move the needle, and passes behind the line, mostly screens, are a net loss at -0.146 with a -13 CPOE. That is an offense that can't block on the perimeter or win in the run game, so its short game doesn't work. Love himself is not the problem there. He is also much better under center (0.337 EPA, +9.3 CPOE) than in shotgun (0.070, -5.7 CPOE). That points to play-action and the defense having to respect the run, even a bad one.

The soft spots are the high-leverage ones. In the red zone he is at -0.208 EPA per play, though he has nine touchdowns there. On third down he sits at 0.005 with a 33.8% conversion rate. In close fourth quarters he is at -0.283 with two picks on 32 plays. Those samples are small, but together they describe a passer who has been explosive between the 20s and inefficient in the moments that compress the field. The bigger concern going forward is the line in front of him. His center is on IR and a starting guard is expected to miss multiple weeks, on a team already 29th in QB hit rate allowed.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep throws carry everything
strengths.body: His passing value comes from throws of 10+ air yards: 0.473 EPA on 10-19 yards and 0.501 on 20+, far above what his short game produces. He has ranked 19th or better in yards per attempt in every full season (7th in 2024), so this has always been his game rather than a hot streak. The 34.1% completion rate on deep balls means it will be streaky week to week, but the value is real.

strengths.title: Volume locked in by the run game
strengths.body: Green Bay's run game is the league's worst by EPA and the offense leans pass-heavy in neutral situations. That keeps him near 40 attempts a game regardless of score. As long as the ground game stays broken, his yardage floor is among the highest at the position.

strengths.title: Accuracy has rebounded lately
strengths.body: His CPOE over the last three games is 5.7 points better than his season mark, and his EPA per dropback has doubled. That fits his history: every full season from 2023 to 2025 had a positive CPOE. The early-season craters look more like a slow start against tough fronts than a new, less accurate quarterback.

concerns.title: Interior line is falling apart
concerns.body: Center Jacob Monk is on IR, and guard Sean Rhyan (87% of snaps) is expected to miss multiple weeks. Tackle Travis Glover, who has played every snap when available, is questionable. This offense already ranks 29th in QB hit rate allowed, and Love's season-opening collapse came under heavy pressure. Replacing two interior starters threatens both the rhythm and the play-action game that make him effective.

concerns.title: Season CPOE still well below his norm
concerns.body: Even with the rebound, his season CPOE is 34th and 7.9 points below last year. His bad-throw rate is up to 14.8%, though that is closer to his 2023-24 levels than last year's 12.5% was. Part of the gap is the broken screen game, where a -13 CPOE behind the line drags down the total. 2025's precision may simply have been his peak.

concerns.title: Struggles when the field shrinks
concerns.body: His red-zone EPA is -0.208, third-down EPA is essentially zero, and close fourth quarters have been negative. None of these samples is large. Still, they are the situations where his explosive downfield game has the least room, and they help explain a 4-3 record with this much yardage. Expect the red-zone number to drift up, since nine touchdowns there suggests the efficiency figure is harsher than reality.

trend.note: His passing EPA went -2.7 and -3.2 in the first two games, then positive every week since: 3.6, 6.9, 16.9, 6.1 and 6.9. The last two came against bottom-two defenses, so the climb is real but flattered.

nextGame.headline: Weak Carolina rush meets a patched-up Packers line on short rest
nextGame.body:
Carolina is a middling pass defense (16th in EPA allowed) with one of the league's weaker pass rushes, 28th in QB hit rate and 23rd in sack rate. That is exactly the opponent a depleted Green Bay line wants to see. The catch is that the Panthers are second-best at preventing explosive passes, and explosive passes are where Love makes his living. They have also held opposing WR1s 3.3 PPR points under their averages. The softer spots are tight ends and third receivers, which points toward Tucker Kraft and the underneath and seam game. The Book has Green Bay -3.5 at home with a 47.5 total, a fair script for normal passing volume. It is a Thursday game on four days' rest, and his only other short week this season was the Atlanta loss. Gusts in the low 20s could nudge a deep shot or two, but not enough to change the plan.

Availability cuts both ways. Green Bay is without Monk at center and almost certainly Rhyan at guard, Glover is questionable, and the most-targeted receiver, Matthew Golden, missed Monday's practice with shoulder and foot problems. Losing Golden is less damaging than his target volume suggests. He has produced 0.101 EPA per target, against 0.521 for Christian Watson and 0.334 for Kraft, so more volume for those two could actually help efficiency. On Carolina's side, edge-rushing linebacker Jaelan Phillips is out, which thins an already weak rush further. Cornerback Akayleb Evans is questionable after not practicing.

keyMatchups.title: Patched line vs. a toothless rush
keyMatchups.body: Carolina's 28th-ranked hit rate and the absence of Phillips should give Love a cleaner pocket than his line injuries deserve. If the replacement interior holds up, he can work the middle of the field, where he is at 0.513 EPA per attempt. If it doesn't, interior pressure will kill the timing even without a strong edge rush.

keyMatchups.title: Explosive-pass prevention vs. his deep game
keyMatchups.body: Carolina allows the second-lowest explosive pass rate in the league, which directly challenges his 10+ air-yard value. Watson's per-target efficiency is what drives his ceiling. Expect fewer chunk plays and more of the volume that has carried him on quieter days.

keyMatchups.title: Kraft against a soft TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Carolina has allowed above-average production to tight ends and ranks 19th in EPA per TE target. Kraft is already one of Love's most efficient options, and with Golden possibly limited, he is the natural place for extra targets.

nextGame.watch: How often Love is hit through the new interior line on early downs. If he stays clean, the downfield rebound continues even against a defense that limits explosive plays.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume should hold. Nothing in the dossier suggests Green Bay's run game is about to recover, so 35 to 40 attempts a week remains the baseline. His yardage pace of 4,755 is believable, perhaps shading a bit lower if the line injuries force more conservative calls. Efficiency should settle between his ugly start and his recent run. Expect EPA per dropback around last-three levels against average or weak defenses and closer to the season mark against good fronts. CPOE should hover near zero rather than return to last year's +5.5. Red-zone efficiency is the most likely to improve, and the close-game struggles are too small a sample to project forward.

The real risk is protection. Two interior starters are out for weeks, and his week 1 performance under pressure was the worst of his season. His rushing has basically disappeared: about a yard a game after averaging 13.3 last year. The dossier doesn't say why, so don't count on scrambles to bail out a collapsing pocket. His fantasy value rests on passing volume and touchdowns. Project roughly 250 to 295 passing yards a game, which leaves him a strong-floor QB1-to-QB2 type whose ceiling depends on the deep ball landing.
swingFactors: How long Rhyan and Monk are out, and how their replacements hold up
Whether the Packers' run game shows any life
Golden's health and how targets shift to Watson and Kraft

confidence.note: Seven games with a clear early-to-late split. The line injuries add real uncertainty, and many splits rest on 30-50 plays.
